=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1275-1282 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `unknown)` arm of the hold `case` in `unblock_main` logs and returns without patching the hold comment, so its `updated_at` stays at the time the hold was posted.
  WHY: The scan treats the hold marker as stale after `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS` (6) and re-dispatches the judge repeatedly until the hold expires, causing many unnecessary judge runs. Reviewers estimated about 56 to 336 runs, and the `unmet` arm avoids this by patching the comment. All reviewers rated it MAJOR. The estimates differ on run frequency (6-hourly vs about hourly, bounded by the 60-minute in-flight cooldown).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:~1275-1282 (`unblock_main`, hold `case` arm `unknown)`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When a hold's condition cannot be read and the hold is still inside its lifetime, the script logs `outcome=skip reason=hold_check_unavailable` and returns without refreshing the hold comment, so `updated_at` stays at the post time. The `unmet` arm patches the comment.
  WHY: `scripts/unblock_scan.py` skips an item only while its newest trusted `ai:unblock-wait:v1` marker is younger than `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS` (6). The poller feeds `.updated_at // .created_at` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19113`), so the scan re-dispatches the judge on every scan, bounded only by `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_INFLIGHT_MINUTES` (60). That is about 300 runs per item until `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS`.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: in `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`, `unknown)` arm, call `unblock_patch_comment "${hold_id}"` with the "Waiting for …; condition unreadable; last checked ${now}" body and the open marker before `return 0` (about 4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1275-1282 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `unknown` hold condition handler does not update the hold comment's timestamp.
  WHY: `updated_at` stays fixed at the hold's creation time. The poller (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`) uses it, so the hold looks stale after `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS` (6) and is re-dispatched, causing up to about 330 unnecessary judge runs.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1275-1279 (`unblock_main`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When a hold check returns `unknown` before the hold expires, the judge logs and returns without updating the hold comment. The poller uses `updatedAt` as the marker timestamp (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19021–19026`) and dispatches again once it is older than `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS`. The 60-minute recent-run cooldown then permits a dispatch roughly hourly, not the documented six-hour recheck.
  WHY: An unreadable condition, such as a GitHub API failure, leaves the marker stale, so the poller repeatedly starts judge runs until the hold expires. That is about 336 runs over the default 14-day lifetime.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:1275-1282 (`unknown)` arm of the `hold_status` case) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `unknown)` arm returns without patching the hold comment, so `updated_at` stays at the time the hold was posted.
  WHY: After `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_RETRY_HOURS` (6) the scan sees the hold as stale and dispatches the judge again. The judge gets `unknown` again and returns. This repeats every 6 hours until `UNBLOCK_JUDGE_WAIT_MAX_DAYS` (14 days), about 56 unnecessary runs. The `unmet` arm avoids this by calling `unblock_patch_comment`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
